THE GEORGIAN, SWEPT WHOLE: 292 ISSUES, TWO HITS
Sir George Williams University's student newspaper, digitized by Concordia
Records Management and Archives in the rma-concordia-publications collection.
Swept 2026-09-07 under p_463.

=====================================================================
WHY IT HAD TO BE BRUTE FORCE
=====================================================================

sgw-concordia-connection.md has carried an open question since 2026-07-09:
"Are there SGW student newspaper (The Georgian) articles about Camp Kanawana
from the 1930s-1960s?" It could not be answered by search, and now it is known
why: archive.org's advancedsearch.php is METADATA ONLY, its own full-text APIs
are unreachable from this environment, and Open Library's search/inside --
the one full-text route that works here -- INDEXES BOOKS ONLY (f_5371). A
student newspaper is catalogued by date; its contents are outside every index
available.

SO EVERY ISSUE WAS DOWNLOADED AND GREPPED. 292 text items, six workers, each
file deleted after searching. The whole run took a few minutes. The filename
trap applies -- the djvu.txt is named after the item's TITLE, not its
identifier -- and the metadata call gives the right name.

RESULT: 290 issues contain neither camp's name. TWO DO. Both are new to this
project and neither is an article about the camp, which is itself the finding:
what a student newspaper carried was a job advertisement and a retirement
notice.

=====================================================================
HIT 1 -- 20 FEBRUARY 1962, Vol. 25 No. 16
A KANAWANA STAFF ADVERTISEMENT AIMED AT SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS STUDENTS
=====================================================================

The OCR interleaves the advertisement with the sports page beside it, so it is
quoted here in the fragments the text preserves, in order:

  "Summer Employment -- Opportunity for employment with the Montreal YMCA
  Kamp Kanawana -- the Laurentian camp for Boys. Kanawana offers special
  opportunity for training and personal growth through all camp and section
  training programs and regular supervision. An opportunity for working with
  boys through A SYSTEMATIC PROCESS OF PLANNED GROUP DEVELOPMENT under the
  guidance of outstanding educational camp leade[rs] ..."

  "... years plus chauffeur's license -- honorarium $300. Room and Board
  included. Truck Driver
  Camp Dates: June 23rd to August 25th
  A. Ross Seaman, M.Ed. - Director,
  Dr. H. G. Dimock, Co-ordinator of staff training and development,
  Metropolitan YMCA
  APPLY: Director, Kamp Kanawana, 1441 Drummond St."

FIVE THINGS IN IT.

1. THE LINK ITSELF, which is what the open question asked for. The camp
   recruited its staff in the university's student paper. Not an article about
   the camp -- an advertisement placed by it.
2. "A SYSTEMATIC PROCESS OF PLANNED GROUP DEVELOPMENT", in the camp's own
   recruitment prose, in February 1962. This project has P.G.D. from the 1959
   annual report (f_5256) and from the 1961 report's "second season". Here it
   is a third time, in a third document type, and used as a SELLING POINT to
   students rather than described in a report to the board.
3. DR. H. G. DIMOCK as "Co-ordinator of staff training and development,
   Metropolitan YMCA" -- a dated association post, February 1962, the year
   BEFORE he became first Chairman of Applied Social Science at Sir George
   Williams. This project's Dimock article has the 1963 chairmanship and the
   1962 Mistassini Cree study; it does not have this.
4. THE 1962 SEASON'S DATES: June 23rd to August 25th.
5. A WAGE. A truck driver, needing a chauffeur's licence, at an honorarium of
   $300 with room and board -- for a nine-week season. This project holds
   almost no wage or price data after the 1970s and less before.

Seaman as director in 1962 is NOT new -- directors-index.md has him 1959-1968
and says he "again directed the camp" in 1962 -- but "M.Ed." is, and the
advertisement corroborates the directorship from an independent document type.

=====================================================================
HIT 2 -- 3 OCTOBER 1961, Vol. 25 No. 2
"MR. MAC" RETIRES, AND HE IS CLARENCE J. McGERRIGLE
=====================================================================

  "A 'Farewell' to the Y.M.C.A. Camp Otoreke director, 'MR. MAC', was held in
  BUDGE HALL of Central YMCA last Friday evening. Mr. David Walker was in
  charge of the evening's programme[.] Mr. Starkey addressed the large crowd
  of former campers, friends and associates (to whom 'Mr. Mac' has been 'MR.
  CAMP DIRECTOR' FOR OVER 15 YEARS).

  Along with Mr. Starkey's complimentary remarks of the warmth and
  appreciation felt by all who attended was the presentation to 'Mr. Mac' and
  his charming wife, of an 19-inch console model television set. It was quite
  a gala evening -- dancing, buffet, etc. -- with the proceeds going to the
  WORLD SERVICES CAMPAIGN. Mr. Mac has always been known for his terrific
  support of The World Services Campaign.

  May we of the Georgian add to the best wishes for an advan[t]urous
  retirement to a 'great guy.'"

HE IS ALREADY IN THIS WIKI UNDER HIS SURNAME. camp-otoreke.md quotes the 1956
annual report on "Mr. and Mrs. C. J. McGerrigle, who have been associated with
this important undertaking for twenty-one years... Mr. and Mrs. 'MAC' have a
deep interest in young people", and the YMCA Year Book gives "Dir. Camp
Otoreke, Clarence J. McGerrigle" for 1951, 1953 and 1957 through 1961, with
Colin R. McKay in the post from 1963.

WHAT THIS ADDS, AND IT IS THE PIECE THAT WAS MISSING. The Otoreke article says
in as many words that "1962 produced no hit and it was not established whether
the 1962 volume is in the collection, so nothing is claimed about the handover
year." THE HANDOVER YEAR IS NOW DATED: McGerrigle's retirement farewell was
held on the Friday before 3 October 1961, so about 29 SEPTEMBER 1961. He
retired at the end of the 1961 season, and McKay's appearance in the 1963
volume is the succession, not a gap.

IT ALSO DISTINGUISHES TWO SPANS THAT THE 1956 REPORT RUNS TOGETHER. The
association dates from 1935 -- twenty-one years by 1956. But the Georgian says
"Mr. Camp Director for over 15 years", which from 1961 reaches back to about
1946 OR EARLIER. Being associated with a camp and directing it are different
things, and the two sources may be measuring different ones. Nothing is
resolved here; the distinction is recorded.

AND THE SMALL THINGS, which are the sort a report never carries: the farewell
was in BUDGE HALL at Central; DAVID WALKER ran the programme and MR. STARKEY
gave the address; the gift was a nineteen-inch console television to
McGerrigle AND HIS WIFE, who the 1956 report shows had been in it with him
from the start; and the proceeds of the evening went to the WORLD SERVICES
CAMPAIGN, which he was known for supporting -- which is a small, real piece of
character, and connects to the 1939 World Service table that lists Kanawana
and Otoreke as their own contributing units (f_5244).

=====================================================================
ONE OCR TRAP IN THIS ISSUE, WORTH FLAGGING
=====================================================================

The column immediately before the McGerrigle notice ends "Mr. V. McAdam,
Executive Dir-", cut off mid-word by the column break. V. McAdam is an
executive of the BOYS CLUBS OF CANADA in the adjacent story about a Fellowship
orientation weekend at the Seigniory Club, Montebello. He has nothing to do
with Otoreke, and a careless read of the OCR would make him "Mr. Mac".
